geopark_about_araripe: A sedimentary basin in southern Ceará, world-famous for the Early Cretaceous fossils of the Crato and Romualdo formations.
geopark_about_cacapava: Late Precambrian volcanic and sedimentary rocks form towers, hills and waterfalls in the pampas of Rio Grande do Sul, with a long history of copper mining.
geopark_about_caminhos_dos_canions_do_su: Canyons carved into the Serra Geral lava flows on the border between Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina, surrounded by Atlantic Forest.
geopark_about_quarta_colonia: Central Rio Grande do Sul, with Triassic fossils that include some of the world's oldest dinosaurs.
geopark_about_serido: Backlands of Rio Grande do Norte holding some 600 million years of geological history: Precambrian rocks, canyons, ranges and old mines.
geopark_about_uberaba: Late Cretaceous rocks with dinosaur and other vertebrate fossils, and basalt flows, in the Triângulo Mineiro region of Minas Gerais.
geopark_caminhos_dos_canions_do_sul: Caminhos dos Cânions do Sul Geopark (SC/RS)

geoparks_intro: Territories with geological heritage of international significance, recognised by UNESCO and managed through conservation, education and sustainable tourism.
glossary_cat_geomorphological: Striking landforms: ranges, canyons, plateaus, inselbergs, waterfalls.
glossary_cat_historical: Places tied to the history of geology or mining, such as old mines.
glossary_cat_hydrogeological: Groundwater and where it shows, such as springs and aquifers.
glossary_cat_igneous: Rocks formed as magma cools, deep underground (plutonism) or at the surface (volcanism).
glossary_cat_impact: Astrobleme: a crater made by a meteorite impact, often heavily eroded.
glossary_cat_marine: Features tied to the sea and coast, such as reefs, cliffs and marine terraces.
glossary_cat_metallogenic: Metal ore deposits and the processes that formed them.
glossary_cat_metamorphic: Rocks transformed by heat and pressure inside the Earth.
glossary_cat_mineralogical: Rare, well-formed or scientifically interesting minerals.
glossary_cat_paleoenvironmental: Records of ancient environments and climates, such as deserts, lakes or seas that no longer exist.
glossary_cat_paleontological: Fossils that matter for understanding past life.
glossary_cat_pedological: Soils of interest for how they formed or their features.
glossary_cat_petrological: Rocks of interest for their composition, texture or origin.
glossary_cat_sedimentological: Sedimentary rocks and structures that show how sediment was carried and laid down, such as bedding and ripple marks.
glossary_cat_stratigraphic: Successions of rock layers that show the order and age of geological events.
glossary_cat_tectonic: Structures from the deformation of the crust, such as faults, folds and shear zones.
glossary_def_approximate: Fragile caves and fossil deposits are shown with their position rounded to about 1 km, so as not to make damage or illegal collecting easier.
glossary_def_degradation_risk: GEOSSIT's low, medium or high rating of how much the site risks being lost, and so how urgently it needs protection.
glossary_def_formation: A body of rock layers with distinctive features that can be mapped and is named after a place, such as the Santana Formation. Formations combine into groups and divide into members; all are lithostratigraphic units.
glossary_def_fossil: The remains or traces of a living thing preserved in rock, such as bones, shells, leaves or imprints.
glossary_def_genus: The rank in the classification of living things just above species. The fossils page groups records by genus, following the GBIF classification.
glossary_def_geodiversity: The variety of rocks, minerals, fossils, soils, landforms and geological processes in a place.
glossary_def_geodiversity_site: A place whose geodiversity is valuable mainly for education, tourism or culture rather than for science.
glossary_def_geologic_map: A map of the rock units exposed at the surface. At 1:1,000,000, the scale this site's ages come from, each unit covers a large area, so the rock mapped at a point may not be exactly what the geosite shows.
glossary_def_geopark: An area recognised by UNESCO for geological heritage of international significance, managed with local communities for conservation, education and sustainable development.
glossary_def_geosite: A place where geodiversity has high scientific value, such as an outcrop, a cave or a fossil deposit that helps tell the Earth's history. In GEOSSIT, geosites are of international or national relevance.
glossary_def_geossit: The Geological Survey of Brazil's (SGB) system for registering and assessing geosites and geodiversity sites. It is the source of this site's geosites.
glossary_def_ichnofossil: A trace of an organism's activity rather than its body: footprints, trackways, burrows, nests or coprolites (fossil dung). The dinosaur footprints of the Rio do Peixe Basin, in Paraíba, are trace fossils.
glossary_def_karst: Landscape formed where water dissolves soluble rocks, mostly limestone, with caves, sinkholes and underground rivers.
glossary_def_outcrop: A place where rock is exposed at the surface, without soil or plants covering it, so it can be seen and studied.
glossary_def_period: The Earth's history is divided into eras and periods, such as the Cretaceous, from 145 to 66 million years ago. Ma means millions of years ago. The colours follow the International Commission on Stratigraphy's chart.
glossary_def_score_didactic: A mark from 0 to 400 for use in education: how well the site illustrates geological concepts, plus access and safety for groups.
glossary_def_score_scientific: A mark from 0 to 400 for the site's interest to science, with criteria such as representativeness, rarity, integrity and published scientific knowledge.
glossary_def_score_tourism: A mark from 0 to 400 for tourism use, with criteria such as scenic beauty, access, safety and nearby facilities.
glossary_def_score_vulnerability: A mark from 0 to 400 for how likely the site is to be damaged, by natural or human causes. The higher, the more fragile.
